The best loan officers won’t make more calls. They’ll create more conversations. That’s the 80/20 flip for mortgage servicing. 80% of borrower outreach is routine: reminders, escrow questions, payoff requests, document status, hardship triage. Voice AI can handle that layer with a fraction of the effort — proactively, compliantly, and at scale. The result is not “more automation.” It's more value conversations for MLOs to step into. AI does the chase. Humans build trust. That’s how servicing teams get 80% more activity without 80% more headcount. ...more ...more

Excited to share that Flair Labs is partnering with Optimum First Mortgage to bring AI voice agents into their lending workflow. Every missed call, delayed follow-up, or unanswered borrower question can be the difference between earning trust and losing momentum. And yet loan officers and teams are often buried under repetitive outreach, status updates, reminders, and qualification calls — work that matters, but doesn’t always need to consume their entire day. Our goal isn’t to replace the human side of lending. It’s to protect it. With Optimum Mortgage, we’re excited to help their team respond faster, engage more borrowers, and create a smoother experience from first conversation to funded loan. ...more ...more

#CVPR2026 (IEEE Technical Community on Pattern Analysis & Machine Intelligence Art Award winner) When Andrej Karpathy reproduced Yann LeCun 's 1989 network in 2022, his conclusion was that almost nothing had changed at the macro level. We still build neural networks the same way LeCun did, layers trained end to end with backpropagation, only now they are vastly bigger. Everything since has been a refinement of that 1989 template. So we rebuilt the template itself, LeNet-1, to point at the original instance of a pattern rather than one of its descendants. We rebuilt it faithfully from LeCun et al.'s NeurIPS 1989 paper, the same network he once demoed on a Bell Labs workstation, and translated only its substrate, bits into atoms. The matrices became transparent PCBs, the activations became brightness, the architecture became spatial depth you can walk around. “artefact(s): LeNet-1 (2026)” might be the oldest question we have made visible. What does it look like when something <thinks>? The work has been accepted to the CVPR 2026 Arts track and spotlighted, one of 12 works chosen from 114. Our thanks to Luba Elliott , who curated the track. We also extend our sincere thanks to Gang Hua , Chair of the #IEEE Computer Society Technical Community on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (TCPAMI), for the Art Award recognizing our work. 🔗 Project LINK: https://lnkd.in/dgsMs-3w
